doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: School music programs and high school in Port Chester
summary: Betts credits school music systems: harmony classes, bands, jazz band playing swing arrangements, student-written plays; he directed the choir and graduated in 1946.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well we heard a good selection of tunes last night with Jazz at the Philharmonic. You come from an area of the country that I think probably offered some jazz opportunity when you grew up.

Well I think one of the basic things that helped me was the school system, because I know in New York State and Pennsylvania and Michigan, they have, at least at that time, they had music in most of the schools, and this helps a great deal, those who want to be musicians because when we were in high school we had Harmony I, Harmony II, Theory I, Theory II, we had a marching band, we had a concert band, and there was tradition for an after school jazz band and those were playing Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey and Jimmy Lunceford and Count Basie arrangements. And they used to put on a play once a year, and the students wrote the music, did the scenery and the whole thing. And

so that was a great help and I was fortunately elected to be the director of the choir for the last two years, for just the high school. And I ended up being Class Musician. So this year, I came out in ‘46, and we’re having our fiftieth reunion this year, and I’m looking forward to it.
There’s nothing like leading a group to really get some experience.
